newsitem.title: GERMANY: Waigel says '97 deficit won't exceed 3 pct of GDP.
newsitem.headline: Waigel says '97 deficit won't exceed 3 pct of GDP.

text.p: Finance Minister Theo Waigel said on Wednesday he did not expect Germany's budget deficit to exceed the Maastricht treaty limit of three percent of gross domestic product this year.

"From today's point of view, the public sector deficit will not exceed three percent of GDP," Waigel said in a statement issued jointly with Christian Democrat (CDU/CSU) regional finance ministers after the finance planning council met.
The finance planning council, which meets twice a year, is a consultative body grouping representatives from federal and municipal governments. The Bundesbank sends an observer.

Waigel's statement diverged from a text issued by the majority of federal states ruled by opposition Social Democrats (SPD), who warned of "excessive" budget deficits this year and next and said government finances may not be sustainable.
Waigel lashed out at what he called the SPD's "obstruction policy" which was holding up efforts to consolidate the budget.
"The SPD is endangering what has worked in the past as a proven cross-party coordinating mechanism," he said.
